timedatectl / journalctl / curl / powershell.exe answers for the Windows Time guard - CAPTURED, not synthetic.

Source:   WSL distro "Ubuntu" (24.04, systemd 255) on the owner's machine, as the unprivileged user, and the Windows
          host's own Windows PowerShell 5.1 (unelevated), on 2026-10-08 between 08:58:11Z and 08:58:31Z, about an hour
          after the w32time incident (research/2026-10-08_windows_time_stopped.md) - w32time running again, StartType
          still Manual. Read-only commands only, run by an agent from one script file
          (`wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- /bin/sh <absolute path>`), each the exact argv the product builds
          (WslCare.Core.Systemd.SystemdCommands.TimesyncStatus / TimeJumpsBackThisBoot,
          WslCare.Core.Health.HealthCommands.ClockReference("https://www.microsoft.com", 10)); the probe's script
          (HealthCommands.ClockScript) was run on the Windows side from a .ps1 file holding the same text.

Files:
  timedatectl-timesync-status.out  timedatectl timesync-status   (Offset -60.856ms, poll interval still the 32 s minimum)
  journalctl-time-jumps.out        journalctl --boot --no-pager --quiet --output=short-monotonic --unit=systemd-journald
                                   --grep=Time jumped backwards  (28 lines, monotonic 34.98 s .. 869.19 s - the fight of
                                   this boot, about 33 s apart, until w32time synced; one line carries journald's own
                                   "(Dropped 1 similar message(s))")
  curl-head-microsoft.out          curl --disable ... --head ... --url https://www.microsoft.com   (HTTP/2 200, Date
                                   08:58:11 GMT against the distro's 08:58:12.03Z taken right after)
  powershell-clock.out             powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command <ClockScript>  (Running, Manual)
  proc-uptime.txt                  /proc/uptime at the capture (4270.67 s)
  captured-at.txt                  the distro's clock at the capture

Redacted, by hand, and nothing else changed:
  - journalctl-time-jumps.out: the host name -> "host"
  - powershell-clock.out: the Windows user name in the profile path -> C:\Users\user
  - every file: CR removed (curl prints CRLF header lines; the parsers trim each line)
